concept.body: SOH-CAH-TOA names three ratios measured from the chosen angle θ: Sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite/Adjacent. Opposite = the leg across from θ; adjacent = the leg touching θ (not the hypotenuse). Identify the sides FIRST, then pick the ratio.

check.body: Name the sides, then the ratio.
explanationVariants: SOH: the side across from θ (6) over the hypotenuse (10) is 0.6.

widget.prompt: Right triangle with legs 6 and 8, hypotenuse 10; θ has opposite side 6. sin θ = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.8 = 8/10 uses the ADJACENT leg — that's cosine. Sine wants the opposite: 6/10 = 0.6.
0.75 = 6/8 is tangent (leg over leg). Sine divides by the hypotenuse: 6/10 = 0.6.

concept.body: A trig ratio is a property of the ANGLE, not of any one triangle. All right triangles sharing an acute angle are similar (AA), so opposite/hypotenuse, adjacent/hypotenuse, and opposite/adjacent each come out identical at every size. Doubling a triangle doubles both sides in a ratio — the quotient doesn't move.

explanationVariants: Both sides scale by the same factor, so the quotient is unchanged: still 0.6.
The doubled triangle is similar to the original; sin θ stays 0.6.

widget.prompt: A right triangle has sin θ = 0.6. Every side is then doubled. Now sin θ = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 1.2 doubles the RATIO — but both sides doubled, so the quotient is untouched: 0.6.
0.3 halves it — same mistake mirrored. Scaling a triangle never changes its angles' ratios: 0.6.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Similar triangles: sin θ is still 0.6.

steps.body: Here's the payoff of similarity. Every right triangle with a 35° angle is similar to every other (AA: right angle + 35°). Similar triangles have proportional sides — so the ratio **opposite ÷ hypotenuse** comes out the SAME in all of them: about 0.574. The angle alone fixes the ratio. That guaranteed constant is called **sin 35°**.

widget.prompt: Three right triangles share a 35° angle but have different sizes. Resize this one and watch whether opp/hyp actually changes.
widget.scaleFeedback: Resize the triangle first — drag the scale dial a couple of times before checking. Until you have, you haven't actually tested whether the ratio depends on size.
widget.successFeedback: 35°, and every resize left opp/hyp exactly where it was. The three triangles in the prompt — hypotenuses 70, 110, 150 — are this same fact at three different scales: the angle fixes the ratio, and size never enters.
widget.lowFeedback: opp/hyp is still under the target — open the angle further.
widget.highFeedback: opp/hyp has gone past the target — close the angle a little.

predict.prompt: Three right triangles all hold a 35° angle, with hypotenuses 70, 110, and 150. Across the three, opposite ÷ hypotenuse will…

options.label: Match exactly — same angle, same shape

predict.reveal: The 35° (plus the right angle) fixes the SHAPE — all three are similar by AA. Scaling multiplies opposite and hypotenuse by the same factor, which cancels in the ratio. That constancy is precisely what lets 'sin 35°' name a single number.

steps.body: Three side-pairs, three named ratios, all measured FROM the chosen acute angle θ: **sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse. cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse. tan θ = opposite/adjacent.** The mnemonic **SOH-CAH-TOA** packs all three. In a 3-4-5 right triangle, sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5, and tan θ = 3/4. “Opposite” is the leg across from θ; “adjacent” is the leg touching θ; the hypotenuse never changes roles.

explanationVariants: Opposite θ is 3, hypotenuse is 5: sin θ = 3/5 = 0.6.

widget.prompt: In a 3-4-5 right triangle, θ is the angle whose opposite side is 3. What is sin θ (as a decimal)?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.8 = 4/5 is cos θ (adjacent over hypotenuse). Sine takes the OPPOSITE side: 3/5 = 0.6.
0.75 = 3/4 is tan θ (opposite over adjacent). Sine divides by the HYPOTENUSE: 3/5 = 0.6.
1.67 ≈ 5/3 flips the fraction. Sine puts the hypotenuse on the BOTTOM: 3/5 = 0.6.

explanationVariants: Adjacent to θ is 4, hypotenuse 5: cos θ = 4/5 = 0.8 — and tan θ = 3/4 = 0.75.

widget.prompt: Same triangle (opposite 3, adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5): what is cos θ?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.6 = 3/5 is sin θ. Cosine takes the ADJACENT side over the hypotenuse: 4/5 = 0.8.
1.33 ≈ 4/3 is adjacent over opposite — an inverted tangent, not a named ratio here. cos θ = 4/5 = 0.8.
0.75 = 3/4 is tan θ. Cosine divides adjacent by the HYPOTENUSE: 4/5 = 0.8.

steps.body: “Opposite” and “adjacent” are relative to WHICH angle you pick — switch to the other acute angle and the two legs swap roles. So sin of one acute angle equals cos of the other. Special angles you already own: tan 45° = 1 (equal legs), sin 30° = 1/2 (short leg over hypotenuse: 1/2).

widget.prompt: In the 3-4-5 triangle, φ is the OTHER acute angle (its opposite side is 4). What is sin φ?

options.label: 4/5 — the roles swap, so sin φ = cos θ
options.feedback: From φ's seat, the 4 is opposite: sin φ = 4/5 = 0.8, exactly the cos of the first angle.

options.label: 3/5 — sine is always the smaller leg over 5
options.feedback: Sine isn't pinned to the smaller leg — it's pinned to the leg OPPOSITE your angle. For φ that's 4, so 4/5.

options.label: 5/4 — the hypotenuse goes on top for the second angle
options.feedback: The hypotenuse stays on the bottom for sine no matter which angle: sin φ = 4/5.

options.label: It can't be computed without a calculator
options.feedback: A calculator is never needed here: read the sides. Opposite φ is 4, hypotenuse 5 → sin φ = 4/5.

explanationVariants: tan 45° compares the two equal legs of a 45-45-90 triangle: 1/1 = 1.
In 45-45-90 the opposite and adjacent legs match, so their ratio — the tangent — is exactly 1.

widget.prompt: Using the 45-45-90 ratio (legs 1, 1, hypotenuse √2): what is tan 45° exactly?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.71 ≈ 1/√2 is sin 45° (leg over hypotenuse). Tangent is leg over LEG: 1/1 = 1.
1.41 ≈ √2 is the hypotenuse-to-leg ratio. tan = opposite/adjacent = 1/1 = 1.
2 doubles a leg — a 30-60-90 reflex. Here the legs are equal, so tan 45° = 1.

steps.body: A fresh triangle, all three ratios.
hints: Identify the sides from θ: opposite = 5, adjacent = 12, hypotenuse = 13.
tan θ = 5/12 — evaluate to 4 decimal places.

widget.prompt: In a 5-12-13 right triangle, θ has opposite side 5. What is tan θ (4 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.3846 ≈ 5/13 is sin θ (over the hypotenuse). Tangent stays among the LEGS: 5/12 ≈ 0.4167.
2.4 = 12/5 flips the fraction: that's tan of the OTHER acute angle. For θ: 5/12 ≈ 0.4167.

takeaways: Similar right triangles (AA) make each side ratio depend on the ANGLE alone.
SOH-CAH-TOA: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj — all measured from θ.
Swap acute angles and opposite/adjacent swap: sin of one = cos of the other.
steps.teaser: Next: use these ratios to SOLVE right triangles — unknown sides first, then unknown angles.
